accepted.question: Describe the structural characteristics, advantages, and disadvantages of Access Control Lists (ACL), Access Control Matrices (ACM), and Capabilities as access control mechanisms.

marking_points.point: Access control structures are defined as mechanisms for implementing access policies, including ACM, Capabilities, and ACLs.
marking_points.quote: Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies: access control matrix (ACM) Capabilities (C-List) access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.quote: ACM is a basic control structure. Advantages: clarity of deﬁnition easy to verify

marking_points.point: A key disadvantage of the Access Control Matrix is its poor scalability and poor handling of changes within the system.
marking_points.quote: Disadvantages: poor scalability poor handling of changes

marking_points.point: An Access Control List (ACL) provides an object-centered description of access rights, listing permissions for specific subjects.
marking_points.quote: ACL is an object-centered description of access rights: bill.doc: {Bob: read, write}

marking_points.point: Disadvantages of ACLs include a poor overview of access rights per subject and difficulty regarding revocation and sharing.
marking_points.quote: Disadvantages: poor overview of access rights per subject difﬁculty of revocation difﬁculty of sharing

marking_points.point: From a design perspective, access control systems utilizing these structures can be classified into discretionary, mandatory, and role-based models.
marking_points.quote: From the design point of view, access control systems can be classiﬁed into discretionary (DAC), mandatory (MAC) and role-based (RBAC).

questions.question: Explain six distinct characteristics regarding the propagation mechanisms, infection techniques, or operational impacts of historical malware and modern web-based worms.

marking_points.point: The Elk Cloner malware propagated by infecting the boot sector of storage media.
marking_points.quote: A program spread via boot sector infection

marking_points.point: The Morris worm utilized a specific debugging feature in sendmail to achieve remote code execution for propagation.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: Executable COM viruses propagate by appending their code to a host program and saving the original entry point.
marking_points.quote: Append a virus body to a program Save an entry point to a program in a virus body

marking_points.point: Executable EXE viruses propagate by overwriting the program header to redirect execution flow to the virus code.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: The Samy worm propagated on MySpace by injecting JavaScript into user profiles which then infected visitors.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript

marking_points.point: Rootkits are designed to mask malicious processes to ensure the attacker maintains privileged remote access.
marking_points.quote: Rootkits are a type of malware that mask malicious processes and software in the infected systems to ensure privileged remote access.

questions.question: State SIX (6) functions or characteristics of preventive network security mechanisms, specifically focusing on firewalls, proxy servers, network segmentation, VPNs, Zero Trust access, and intrusion prevention systems.

marking_points.point: Firewalls control traffic based on predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Proxy servers act as firewalls and web filters to improve data security.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation creates boundaries between segments with common functions or risks.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: Remote Access VPNs provide secure remote access to the organization network.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access ensures users only have permissions required for their role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: IDS/IPS detect or prevent attacks such as brute force and Denial-of-Service.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Discuss six specific obligations of a computing professional under the ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct regarding their duties to society, clients, and the profession.

marking_points.point: Professionals must contribute positively to society and human well-being, recognizing that all people are stakeholders in computing.
marking_points.quote: Contribute to society and to human well-being, acknowledging that all people are stakeholders in computing.

marking_points.point: Professionals are obligated to avoid causing harm through their professional activities and decisions.
marking_points.quote: Avoid harm.

marking_points.point: Professionals must respect the privacy of individuals and handle personal data with care.
marking_points.quote: Respect privacy.

marking_points.point: Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of their professional work.
marking_points.quote: Strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.

marking_points.point: Professionals must maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice throughout their career.
marking_points.quote: Maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.

marking_points.point: Professionals are required to perform work only in areas where they have demonstrated competence.
marking_points.quote: Perform work only in areas of competence.

questions.question: Describe the structural characteristics, advantages, and disadvantages of Access Control Lists (ACL), Access Control Matrices (ACM), and Capabilities as access control mechanisms.

marking_points.point: Access control structures are defined as mechanisms for implementing access policies, including ACM, Capabilities, and ACLs.
marking_points.quote: Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies: access control matrix (ACM) Capabilities (C-List) access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.point: The Access Control Matrix (ACM) is considered a basic control structure that offers clarity of definition and is easy to verify.
marking_points.quote: ACM is a basic control structure. Advantages: clarity of deﬁnition easy to verify

marking_points.point: A key disadvantage of the Access Control Matrix is its poor scalability and poor handling of changes within the system.
marking_points.quote: Disadvantages: poor scalability poor handling of changes

marking_points.point: An Access Control List (ACL) provides an object-centered description of access rights, listing permissions for specific subjects.
marking_points.quote: ACL is an object-centered description of access rights: bill.doc: {Bob: read, write}

marking_points.point: Disadvantages of ACLs include a poor overview of access rights per subject and difficulty regarding revocation and sharing.
marking_points.quote: Disadvantages: poor overview of access rights per subject difﬁculty of revocation difﬁculty of sharing

marking_points.point: From a design perspective, access control systems utilizing these structures can be classified into discretionary, mandatory, and role-based models.
marking_points.quote: From the design point of view, access control systems can be classiﬁed into discretionary (DAC), mandatory (MAC) and role-based (RBAC).

questions.question: Describe six key characteristics or components of Windows security mechanisms regarding subjects, access rights, directory services, and system complexity.

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are defined as active entities such as processes and threads.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads.

marking_points.point: Security credentials for a subject are stored within a token.
marking_points.quote: Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: Access rights describe what actions can be performed on an object and are encoded as a 32-bit mask.
marking_points.quote: Encoded as a 32-bit mask

marking_points.point: Standard access rights include the ability to read an object’s security descriptor.
marking_points.quote: READ_CONTROL: read object’s security descriptor

marking_points.point: Active Directory serves as a directory service for organizing system resources like users, groups, and security policies.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources

marking_points.point: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms can lead to severe security incidents due to misconfiguration or bugs.
marking_points.quote: The complexity of Windows security mechanisms is also its enemy: misconﬁguration as well as implementation bugs may lead to severe security incidents.

questions.question: Discuss the classification of biometric mechanisms into psychological and behavioural categories, providing specific examples for each type as presented in the lecture materials.

marking_points.point: Biometric applications are categorized into two distinct sectors.
marking_points.quote: Biometric applications available today are categorized into 2 sectors

marking_points.point: Psychological biometrics include characteristics such as iris, fingerprints, hand, retinal, and face recognition.
marking_points.quote: Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition

marking_points.point: Behavioural biometrics include characteristics such as voice, typing pattern, and signature.
marking_points.quote: Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

marking_points.point: Retinal scanning involves scanning the retina into a database using low intensity light while the user looks straight into the reader.
marking_points.quote: User looks straight into retinal reader Scan using low intensity light

marking_points.point: Iris scanning captures the unique pattern of the iris, which is coloured and visible from a distance without requiring physical contact.
marking_points.quote: Scans unique pattern of iris Iris is coloured and visible from far No touch required

marking_points.point: Fingerprint recognition faces disadvantages such as issues with dirt, grime, wounds, and the potential for spoofing, making liveness detection important.
marking_points.quote: Dirt , grime and wounds Can be spoofed – liveness important!

questions.question: Explain six distinct characteristics regarding the nature of threats, attacks, and security objectives in the context of malware and system vulnerabilities.

marking_points.point: A threat is defined as a potential violation of security rather than an actual event.
marking_points.quote: Threats: A threat is a “potential” violation of security

marking_points.point: An attack is characterized as the actual violation of security that exploits vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: Attacks: The actual violation of security

marking_points.point: A vulnerability is identified as a weakness within a system that can be exploited to cause damage.
marking_points.quote: Vulnerabilities: Weakness of a system that can be exploited to damage assets

marking_points.point: Confidentiality is a security objective ensuring that no information has been inappropriately disclosed.
marking_points.quote: Conﬁdentiality: no information has been inappropriately disclosed

marking_points.point: Integrity is a security objective ensuring that data has not been maliciously altered.
marking_points.quote: Integrity: data has not been (maliciously) altered

marking_points.point: Availability is a security objective ensuring that data and services can be accessed as desired by users.
marking_points.quote: Availability: data/services can be accessed as desired

marking_points.point: The Nexus acts as a security kernel that is authenticated during the boot process.
marking_points.quote: NGSCB: Nexus Security kernel, authenticated on boot

marking_points.point: The Nexus is responsible for authenticating trusted programs before they execute.
marking_points.quote: Authenticates trusted programs Application interface to TPM

marking_points.point: The Nexus serves as the application interface to the Trusted Platform Module (TPM).

marking_points.point: The Nexus operates without trusting the standard operating system.

marking_points.point: The NCA is a trusted software component that runs in a trusted mode.

questions.question: Explain the mechanisms of Single Sign-On, Kerberos user login, and smart cards as alternative authentication methods in distributed environments.

marking_points.point: Single Sign-On reduces the burden on users by minimizing the need to remember multiple passwords.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the need to memorize passwords

marking_points.point: SSO solutions can be implemented using client-server architectures such as Kerberos or Active Directory.
marking_points.quote: Client-server architectures (Kerberos, Active Directory)

marking_points.point: During Kerberos login, the hash value of the user's password serves as the secret key for the client.
marking_points.quote: The hash value of his password KU = h(P) becomes a secret key of the client/user.

marking_points.point: Smart cards are recognized as an alternative mechanism to passwords for verifying user identity.
marking_points.quote: Alternative user authentication mechanisms are smart cards, biometric methods and two-factor authentication.

marking_points.point: Kerberos is specifically designed to automate the authentication process within large distributed systems.
marking_points.quote: Single sign-on methods such as Kerberos provide means for automating authentication in large distributed environments.

marking_points.point: Windows 2000 introduced significant security milestones including the integration of Kerberos and Active Directory.
marking_points.quote: Windows 2000: Active Directory, Kerberos, security architecture.
